description: §4.12 + §38.1 — a `<channel>` inside a NESTED `<program name=>` fires E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-NESTED-PROGRAM. Regression pin for g-nested-program-emits-artifacts-it-never-produces: pre-fix this shape compiled EXIT 0 and shipped a client that dialled `/_scrml_ws/nested_feed` against a route no server ever mounted, reconnecting silently every 2 seconds forever. The mechanism was a stale analysis snapshot — `analyzeAll` caches `channelNodes` by object reference BEFORE the §4.12.4 worker-extraction pre-pass splices the nested subtree out, so the CLIENT emitter (reading the cache) emitted the connection while the SERVER emitter (walking the live post-splice tree) emitted no route. The canonical sibling `<channel name="canonical-feed">` directly under the top-level `<program>` is unaffected and must NOT draw a placement diagnostic.
rationale: §38.1 invariant 1 and the §38.2 normative list both state: "A `<channel>` inside a NESTED `<program name=>` (§4.12) SHALL emit E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-NESTED-PROGRAM." §4.12.1 is the reason: "A nested `<program>` SHALL be a separate compilation unit" — the compiler extracts the subtree before server emission, so the channel's server-side WebSocket upgrade route is never emitted, and the §4.12.4 worker bundle carries no channel code either (a worker bundle compiles only function declarations and the `when message` hook). Emitting the client half alone is a connection to a route that does not exist. No runtime half: the source is REJECTED at compile time. Contrast `channel/inside-scoped-db-program` (the §4.12.6 shape that is NOT extracted and does NOT fire) and `channel/inside-page` / `channel/outside-program` (the other two placement violations).
